instrument_name: 49 U.S.C. 14503 Withholding State and local income tax by certain carriers (US Code 2024 ed., GPO govinfo)
figure_or_rule_carried: Motor carrier / motor private carrier employee with regularly assigned duties in 2 or more States with respect to a motor vehicle: compensation taxable ONLY by the State and subdivision of residence; carrier files information returns only with residence State/subdivision; water carriers file with residence State and the State where more than 50% of prior-year pay was earned (more than 50% of time worked). Replaces the LII republication row US-FED-P5-1-007 as the source copy (same instrument, official text).

instrument_name: 49 U.S.C. 11502 Withholding State and local income tax by rail carriers (US Code 2024 ed., GPO govinfo)
figure_or_rule_carried: Rail-carrier employee with regularly assigned duties on a railroad in more than one State: compensation taxable only by the State/subdivision of residence; carrier files information returns only there. Replaces LII row US-FED-P5-1-008 as the source copy.

instrument_name: 49 U.S.C. 40116(f) Pay of air carrier employees (US Code 2024 ed., GPO govinfo)
figure_or_rule_carried: Air carrier employee with regularly assigned duties on aircraft in at least 2 States: pay taxable only by (A) the residence State/subdivision and (B) the State/subdivision where the employee earns more than 50% of carrier pay (deemed where scheduled flight time is more than 50% of total for the calendar year); (f)(3) union-leave pay follows the same rule (Pub. L. 115-254, 2018).

instrument_name: 46 U.S.C. 11108 Taxes (seamen) (US Code 2024 ed., GPO govinfo)
figure_or_rule_carried: (a) Wages of a master or seaman on a vessel in foreign, coastwise, intercoastal, interstate or noncontiguous trade, or of an individual on a fishing or fish-processing vessel, may NOT be withheld under State or local tax laws (a voluntary agreement is allowed only for coastwise trade between ports of the same State). (b) Pilots with duties in more than one State and masters/officers/crew with regular duties on vessels on navigable waters of 2 or more States: taxable only by the State/subdivision of residence.

instrument_name: 50 U.S.C. 4001 Residence for tax purposes (SCRA sec. 511, as amended by Pub. L. 115-407 (2018) and Pub. L. 117-333 (2023)) (US Code 2024 ed.)
figure_or_rule_carried: A military spouse present in a State solely to be with the servicemember under military orders neither loses nor acquires residence; income for the spouse's services is not sourced to that State if the spouse is not resident there (c); for any taxable year the couple may elect as residence the servicemember's residence, the spouse's residence, or the servicemember's permanent duty station (a)(3); military pay is not sourced to the duty State of a nonresident servicemember (b). Payroll effect: work-State withholding stops on the State's exemption certificate (e.g. WV/IT-104, DC D-4A, CA DE 4 box).

instrument_name: 42 U.S.C. 653a(b) National new-hire reporting: multistate employers and timing (US Code 2024 ed.)
figure_or_rule_carried: An employer with employees in 2 or more States that reports magnetically or electronically may designate ONE State in which it has employees to receive all its new-hire reports, notifying the Secretary (HHS) in writing; timing: each State sets it, but not later than 20 days after hire, or by 2 monthly electronic transmissions not less than 12 nor more than 16 days apart.

instrument_name: 42 U.S.C. 666(b)(6)(A), (b)(9), (f) Income withholding: orders from another State (US Code 2024 ed.)
figure_or_rule_carried: An employer receiving an income withholding order issued by ANOTHER State applies the income withholding law of the State of the obligor's PRINCIPAL PLACE OF EMPLOYMENT for (I) the employer fee, (II) the maximum amount withheld, (III) the implementation and remittance time periods, (IV) priorities among multiple child-support obligees, and (V) terms not in the order; pays the SDU within 7 business days; an employer complying with a notice regular on its face has no civil liability; every State must have UIFSA in effect (f).

instrument_name: 29 U.S.C. 218(a) FLSA relation to other laws (US Code 2024 ed.)
figure_or_rule_carried: The FLSA does not excuse noncompliance with a Federal, State or municipal law setting a HIGHER minimum wage, a LOWER maximum workweek or a higher child-labour standard: the employee receives the more protective standard of the place whose law applies (federal floor plus state/local overlay).

instrument_name: 26 U.S.C. 3306(b)(1) FUTA wages: 7,000 per employer per calendar year; successor rule (US Code 2024 ed.)
figure_or_rule_carried: The FUTA wage base of 7,000 USD counts remuneration for employment paid to the individual by the employer in the calendar year: one base per employer, not one per State; a successor that acquires substantially all of a predecessor's trade or business counts the predecessor's pre-acquisition wages. State SUI bases are separate, and each State decides whether wages reported to another State count (example CA CUIC 930.1, US-MULTIS5-010).

instrument_name: California EDD DE 44 Employer Guide Rev. 52 (4-26): Wages in Another State; Interstate Reciprocal Coverage Elections; nonresident apportionment; multistate new hire
article_or_section: p.78 (PDF p.86) Wages in Another State + Interstate Reciprocal Coverage Elections; nonresident table (PIT); New Employee Registry
figure_or_rule_carried: CUIC 930.1: wages paid for employment subject to another State's UI law and reported there count toward the CA UI taxable wage limit in the same calendar year if the individual is later transferred to CA. CUIC 602/603: a worker in 2 or more States whose service is not localized in any one State may, on approval, be reported to one State where services are performed, the employee resides, or the employer has a place of business (UI and SDI). Nonresident working in CA and elsewhere: CA PIT wages = CA working days / total working days (volume-of-business ratio for commission pay). Multistate employers may report all new hires to one State.

instrument_name: General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 (2026): Boxes 15-20 State and local income tax information; Multiple forms; W-3 box 15
article_or_section: Specific Instructions for Form W-2, Boxes 15 through 20; Multiple forms; Form W-3 Box 15, Boxes 16-19
figure_or_rule_carried: W-2 boxes 15-20 carry state and local wages and income tax for up to TWO states and TWO localities (two-letter state code + state-assigned employer ID), each separated by the broken line; for more than two states or localities prepare a second Form W-2 repeating boxes a-f, and never report the same federal tax data to SSA on more than one Copy A; W-3 box 15: enter 'X' and no state ID when the W-2s carry more than one state; W-3 boxes 16-19 = one sum across all states/localities. State/locality reporting specifics: contact each state.

instrument_name: NY DTF FAQ: Filing Requirements, Residency, and Telecommuting for NYS Personal Income Tax
authority: NY State Dept of Taxation and Finance
article_or_section: Q: primary office in NY, telecommuting from outside the state
figure_or_rule_carried: Nonresident whose primary office is in New York State: telecommuting days are NY working days unless the employer has established a bona fide employer office at the telecommuting location; unless the employer specifically acted to establish one, NY tax remains owed on telecommuting income. Gives US-MULTI-003 (no local file) a held copy.

instrument_name: NY DTF TSB-M-06(5)I Application of the Convenience of the Employer Test to Telecommuters and Others (2006-05-15), quoting 20 NYCRR 132.18(a)
authority: NY State Dept of Taxation and Finance
article_or_section: pp.1-2; 20 NYCRR 132.18(a) quoted; bona fide employer office factors
figure_or_rule_carried: 20 NYCRR 132.18(a): a nonresident employee working inside and outside NY allocates compensation by NY working days / total working days; days worked outside NY count only if of NECESSITY, as distinguished from convenience (convenience-of-the-employer test); nonworking days (weekends, holidays, sickness, vacation, leave) excluded from the ratio; a home office counts as out-of-state only when it is a bona fide employer office under the memo's factors.

instrument_name: 61 Pa. Code 109.8 Earnings of nonresident employes or casual employes and officers
figure_or_rule_carried: PA nonresident employee (incl. corporate officers; salesmen under 109.7 excluded) working inside and outside PA: PA-source compensation = PA working days / total working days; days outside PA count only for services that of NECESSITY obligate out-of-state duties (necessity test, the same structure as NY's convenience test); nonworking days excluded. Does not override the PA reciprocal agreements (US-MULTI-007).

instrument_name: Delaware Division of Revenue: 2025 Non-Resident Individual Income Tax Return Instructions (PIT-NON, revised 03/27/26), Line 1 wages / Form PIT-SCW
article_or_section: p.4, wages column B and NOTE on Form PIT-SCW
figure_or_rule_carried: Nonresident with Delaware employment: income for services that the employment REQUIRES to be rendered outside Delaware may be excluded only through Form PIT-SCW apportionment; 'Working from home does not qualify for an exclusion on Form PIT-SCW' (Delaware convenience-type rule; operates at ASSESSMENT on the nonresident return; employer withholding follows the DE employer guide, US-DE-WH-001). Return amounts rounded to whole dollars.

instrument_name: DOL ETA Unemployment Insurance Program Letter No. 20-04 Localization of Work Provisions (2004-05-10)
authority: US DOL Employment and Training Administration
article_or_section: paras 1-7; Attachment I Localization of Work Provisions (attachment not held)
figure_or_rule_carried: Reissues the UIPL 291 (1952) interpretation of the uniform localization-of-work provisions with new examples incl. telecommuting for an employer in another state and long-distance commuting flight attendants; rescissions none, expiration continuing; state law amendments not required for conformity, states encouraged to interpret their laws accordingly. Attachment I (examples) not retrieved: DC DOES republishes it (lead).

instrument_name: DOL OUI memo to State UI Directors: Spirit Airlines, reminder to review localization of work guidance (undated; Acting Deputy Administrator S. Simonetta)
authority: US DOL ETA Office of Unemployment Insurance
figure_or_rule_carried: Current DOL restatement of the localization test, applied in this order: (1) service localized in a State (performed entirely in it, or out-of-state service only incidental: temporary, transitory, isolated); (2) if not localized anywhere, some service in the State of the base of operations; (3) else some service in the State from which service is directed or controlled; (4) else some service in the State of residence. The employee's entire service with that employer is reported to ONE State. Confirms UIPL 20-04 remains the operative guidance.

instrument_name: Ward v. United Airlines, Inc. (Cal. Supreme Court, S248702, 2020-06-29), 9 Cal.5th 732: geographic reach of Labor Code 226
article_or_section: Part III; Part IV answers (1)-(2); Lab. Code 226; Wage Order 9 sec.1(E)
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: in force (final answer to Ninth Circuit certified question). LEVEL: employer pay-statement duty (payroll output), not tax. Rule: Lab. Code 226 (CA itemized wage statement) applies if the employee's PRINCIPAL PLACE OF WORK is in California: works the majority of the time in CA; for interstate transportation workers and others not working a majority anywhere, CA is their base of work operations (e.g. home-base airport) plus some work in CA. Employer location, employee residence, place of pay receipt and payment of taxes are NOT pertinent; a CBA does not oust 226.

instrument_name: Oman v. Delta Air Lines, Inc. (Cal. Supreme Court, S248726, 2020-06-29), 9 Cal.5th 762: reach of Lab. Code 204 and 226 to multistate workers; Sullivan v. Oracle (2011) 51 Cal.4th 1191 as cited
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: in force. LEVEL: employer pay timing and pay statement. (1) Lab. Code 204 (pay-day timing) and 226 do not apply to pay periods in which the employee works in CA only episodically and for less than a day at a time, unless the employee works primarily in CA during the pay period or works primarily in no State and has the base of operations in CA. Application of CA wage-hour law to multistate workers varies statute by statute (Sullivan v. Oracle Corp. (2011) 51 Cal.4th 1191, 1201); employer's nonresident domicile does not exempt it. (3) Geographic reach of the CA minimum wage law left undecided.

instrument_name: S. 1443 (119th Congress) Mobile Workforce State Income Tax Simplification Act of 2025, introduced text (GPO BILLS-119s1443is)
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: DRAFT, NOT ENACTED: introduced 2025-04-10 (Thune, Cortez Masto), read twice and referred to the Senate Committee on Finance; govinfo holds only the introduced (IS) version as of 2026-11-02; congress.gov actions page returned 403. LEVEL: state withholding AND state income taxation of nonresident wages. Would make wages of a multistate employee taxable only by the residence State and a State where the employee is present and working more than 30 days in the calendar year, withholding/reporting from the commencement date; effective 1 January of the second calendar year after enactment (so 2028 at the earliest). Do not model.

instrument_name: Louisiana Act 382 of the 2025 Regular Session (HB 567, enrolled): R.S. 47:112.2(A) and 47:248(B)(1)(a) mobile workforce exemption 30 days; R.S. 47:248(B)(1)(d) repealed
article_or_section: Sec. 1 (R.S. 47:112.2(A), 47:248(B)(1)(a)); Sec. 2 (repeal of 47:248(B)(1)(d)); Sec. 3 (income tax periods beginning on or after 2026-01-01); Sec. 4 (effective on signature; bill page: effective 2025-06-20)
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: in force (Act 382, signed; effective 2025-06-20; applies to income tax periods beginning on or after 2026-01-01). LEVEL: withholding and nonresident taxation. Wages of a nonresident for duties performed in Louisiana for 30 or FEWER days in the calendar year are exempt (was 25 days); the home-State reciprocity condition 47:248(B)(1)(d) is repealed; once the employee's days in LA for the employer and related entities exceed 30, the employer withholds and remits for EVERY day of the year, including the first 30. CONFLICT: LA state rows US-LA-P5-1-001 (active) is silent and the superseded US-LA-P5-1-004 read 'no de minimis rule'; route to the LA unit.

instrument_name: Louisiana Department of Revenue Notice of Intent: Mobile Workforce Exemption (LAC 61:I.1923), amendment implementing Act 382 (2025)
authority: Louisiana Department of Revenue, Tax Policy and Planning Division
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: proposed rule (NOI; comments due 2026-01-26, hearing request deadline 2026-01-10); final adoption in the Louisiana Register NOT verified. LEVEL: withholding and employer reporting. Employer: if a nonresident employee performs duties in LA on more than 30 days, begin withholding and report on Form L-1 starting in the period in which the 31st day falls; the employee's notice to the employer is due within 10 days of the 31st day; the exemption is lost if the nonresident has other LA-source income. The rule as promulgated in 2023 (LR 49:334, 25 days) stands until the amendment is final; the statute (US-MULTIS5-021) governs from 2026-01-01.

instrument_name: Illinois DOR Publication 130 (R-02/26) Who is Required to Withhold Illinois Income Tax: 'When is compensation paid in Illinois' (localization rules 1-4, 30-working-day rule)
article_or_section: pp.3-5 When is compensation paid in Illinois, rules 1-4; examples
figure_or_rule_carried: Illinois sources wage withholding by UI-style LOCALIZATION: (1) all service in IL; (2) out-of-IL service only incidental (temporary, transitory, isolated); (3) IL resident and no rule applies and no other State's tax withheld; (4) service not localized anywhere: withhold on the IL fraction (IL working days / total working days) only if the employee performs significant, nonincidental service in IL on MORE THAN 30 working days. A working day is in IL if more duty time is spent in IL that day (travel excluded) or the only duty is travel arriving in IL; disaster-response days excluded. Example: 35 of 250 days = 14%. Reciprocity carve-out: IA, KY, MI, WI residents and military spouses. Adds the threshold that US-IL-P5-1-001 (same publication) does not carry.

instrument_name: RCW 50A.05.010(8) Washington Paid Family and Medical Leave: definition of employment (localization), effective until 2027-06-30 (Wayback copy 2026-04-23)
figure_or_rule_carried: Washington PFML coverage of a multistate worker follows the UI localization test: an individual's entire service is covered if localized in WA, or not localized anywhere but some service in WA and the base of operations (else the place of direction or control) is in WA, or neither is in a State where service is performed but the residence is in WA; 'service is localized' as in RCW 50.04.120 (the UI law). Pattern: state PFML/SDI programmes key the premium State to the sui_state result (verify per programme in the state units). Live site app.leg.wa.gov returned no connection (curl 000); text read from the Wayback copy.

instrument_name: H.R. 10271 (119th Congress) Mobile Workforce State Income Tax Simplification Act of 2026, introduced text (GPO BILLS-119hr10271ih)
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: DRAFT, NOT ENACTED: introduced 2026-09-03 (Goldman, TX), referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary; House companion of S. 1443 (US-MULTIS5-020) with the same operative text: residence State plus a State of presence for more than 30 days; withholding from the commencement date; effective 1 January of the second calendar year after enactment. LEVEL: state withholding and taxation. Do not model.
